name: WordPress
description: Open source publishing software that powers a large share of the web.
summary: WordPress allows AI tools when writing code, tests, documentation and issues, as long as the contributor understands and tests everything submitted, keeps it GPL-compatible, and discloses meaningful AI assistance in the pull request or Trac ticket. Low-effort, unreviewed AI-generated contributions may be closed, and AI cannot be a contributor or the sole reviewer.

evidence.quote: If you leveraged AI in a meaningful way, please disclose it. For trivial assistance (for example, AI suggests a variable name or reorders imports), disclosure is optional.
- Suggest refactorings or alternative approaches.
Treat AI output like code from an unknown external contributor: you must review and validate it before sharing it.
- Understanding every line of code and documentation you submit.
Once submitted, code contributed by you, regardless of whether it was typed or AI-generated, is considered your code and therefore your responsibility.
When AI meaningfully contributes to your work (beyond trivial reformatting), clearly mention that in your:
- Do not use tools whose terms forbid using their output in GPL-licensed projects or impose additional restrictions on redistribution.
- Do not rely on tools to “launder” incompatible licenses. If an AI output reproduces non-free or incompatible code, it cannot be included.
- You must understand what the code does and why.
- You must run appropriate tests (unit, integration, end-to-end, as applicable).
- You must be able to explain the approach during review.
If a reviewer asks, “What did the AI generate and what did you write?” or “Why is this the right approach?”, you should be able to answer clearly.
